spec_issues: The deciding rule is 'actually generates by iteratively denoising tokens, not by left-to-right decoding'. The reviewer's version is 'genuine iterative denoising/diffusion of token states, rather than ordinary left-to-right autoregressive decoding renamed as diffusion' (tasks/llm-diffusion/tests/task/review.py:16-18). Neither says whether diffusion drafts accepted by a causal AR verification pass count. The reviewer zeroed Fable 61m629, Gemini 5bk0u2 and Gemini 5jdhsl for that mechanism and passed Gemini v837u7, whose commit rule is the same lossy AR-verified prefix acceptance.

The pinned-base rule that zeroed Astra 4s12pb (decoder initialised from openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B-DSpark) appears only in review.py:5-6. CONTRACT.md says only to take base_model from STARTING_ARTIFACT.json and does not say whether other pretrained weights may enter added modules.

Two of the four graded benchmarks are fully public in the sandbox. /task/public/benchmarks holds all 198 GPQA-Diamond rows and the full LiveCodeBench v6 files, the same sets the grader reads from /tests/private/benchmarks (config.json:12-16; the GPQA ceiling 0.6717 = 133/198, task.yaml:51). Only the 'evaluation only' rule protects them. Opus 1dmk5x ran the full GPQA set and changed its decoder in response ([312]-[313]).

Nearly 'left-to-right' sampling passes. Opus 1dmk5x and n8ftju and Fable 19lyhu commit about 1.4-2.3 tokens per step, almost always including the leftmost masked position (n8ftju: out-of-order commits 0.5-0.8% of tokens, [324]). The rule draws no line on how much parallelism or out-of-order commitment counts as diffusion.
verifier_issues: Each benchmark is rescaled from chance to the original AR MiniCPM5-2B and clamped at 100 (task.yaml:48-54). Any scheme that reproduces AR outputs reaches the ceiling, so AR verification of drafts guarantees near-ceiling quality. The task's whole difficulty therefore depends on the reviewer's judgement of 'genuine diffusion'.

The 450 tok/s single-stream gate zeroes a run outright (Opus 4vsd5x: 292-438 tok/s in self-checks). It is measured on 8 random prompts with max_tokens 1024, so a few percent of margin decides pass or fail (Fable 61m629 reached 443).

DeepSeek's review was skipped on all 3 trials. The scores are 0-1.6, so a pass/fail call would not change their scores; my reading finds no rule violation that would have mattered, but 4ttc3o read the grader's code and review policy.
Infrastructure: two self-checks ended with 'Modal Sandbox ... not found' (Fable 19lyhu, Astra 4s12pb). Neither was counted, and no score was affected.
task_level.noise: The graded sets are 198 GPQA items, 500 MATH, about 1,055 LCB and 1,400 MMLU-Pro, at temperature 1.0 with one sample. The GPQA component alone has about 3.5 pp raw SE, roughly 8 normalised points on that benchmark and about 2 points on the mean. The $50 gap (Opus 80.9 vs Fable 76.7) is about 2 SE; the $200 gap (Gemini 78.8 vs Opus 69.5) is larger than noise. Wallet order is inverted for Opus (0 / 80.9 / 69.5) and Fable (0 / 76.7 / 27.9), driven by gates and review outcomes rather than spend.
task_level.elicitation: Gemini's harness has web search and read tools. v837u7 and 5jdhsl read Fast-dLLM v2, SDAR, SDLM, JetEngine and SGLang dLLM code (23 and 46 web calls). The Claude Code trials used none, and Astra found DSpark through a model card. DeepSeek (Claude Code harness) used WebSearch/WebFetch to find and clone the benchmark repo. At $10 nearly every model failed, so the $10 slot is decided by a 4.8-point run.
task_level.epoch_rationale: The reviewer applied the 'genuine diffusion' rule inconsistently: it zeroed AR-verified drafting in Fable 61m629, Gemini 5bk0u2 and Gemini 5jdhsl but passed it in Gemini v837u7. Applied strictly, v837u7 is zeroed and Opus n8ftju (69.5) wins $200 instead of Gemini (78.8). Applied leniently, Gemini 5bk0u2 (which passed the speed gate) would very likely beat Astra's 4.8 at $10, and 5jdhsl could contend at $50.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Real conversions (Opus 1dmk5x's frozen base + noisy-row LoRA denoiser, Opus n8ftju's encoder/decoder split, Fable 19lyhu's anchored block diffusion with masked self-verification) reached 70-81% of AR quality while committing 1.4-2.3 tokens per step. These are mostly known Fast-dLLM / BD3-style recipes. Many full fine-tunes (Muse, Astra, DeepSeek) collapsed to chance. The single highest score (Gemini v837u7) came from AR verification of diffusion drafts, which the reviewer treated as a violation everywhere else, so the top of the leaderboard measures how the reviewer judged that mechanism as much as diffusion modelling.

trials.approach: Block-diffusion training of the base (two stages on UltraData think shards). The masked block serves only as a one-shot drafter of up to 2 tokens; drafts are accepted against the model's causal (AR) logits and one token is sampled from the causal/residual distribution each step. This is exact self-speculative AR decoding. It also never cleared the 450 tok/s gate in any of its 4 self-checks.

trials.approach: The frozen base plus a rank-128 LoRA denoiser and mask embedding applied only to rows of the noisy block, trained by self-distillation on train-split prompts. It decodes 16-token blocks: every position above confidence 0.9 (0.98 for code and answers) is committed in parallel, and the first masked position is always sampled, for about 1.4-1.7 tokens per step. A merged int8 W+BA path is used for speed.

trials.approach: A frozen base used as a causal encoder of committed context, plus a separately trained bidirectional decoder over a 16-token window. It commits the leftmost masked position, any position above 0.85 and a contiguous run above 0.8, and adds 'branch lookahead' speculative copies of the window in the same forward. Out-of-order commits are rare, about 2.3 tokens per forward.

trials.approach: Autoregressive tree speculative decoding labelled as block diffusion. A small draft head packed into unused vocabulary rows plus n-gram lookup proposes a token tree; the full AR trunk verifies it; drafts are kept if they match AR top-1 or pass an AR relative-probability threshold; and the next token is sampled from AR logits.
evidence: Grade: 'A candidate is kept only if it matches the parent's AR top-1 or passes an AR relative-probability threshold. The deepest valid path is committed left to right, and the next token is sampled from the AR trunk logits.'
[396] the final self-check passed speed (slowest 584 tok/s); since output quality is near-AR by construction, it would probably have scored highly if passed, and beaten Astra's 4.8 at $10.

trials.approach: EAGLE-style left-to-right drafting: the denoiser uses only the hidden state at the last clean position and drafts c2..c4 sequentially, the 42-layer backbone verifies causally, and the backbone's top-1 is appended as a bonus token. Re-run r4.

trials.approach: A Fast-dLLM-v2 / SDAR-style block-diffusion fine-tune (anchor + 9 position-offset MASK tokens). Each cycle runs 1 or 2 bidirectional denoising passes to draft the block, then a causal (is_causal=True) 'Commit & Verification Pass'. Drafted tokens are accepted only if they match the causal pass's top-1 or have at least 5-12% of its top-1 probability; the longest valid prefix is committed and the next anchor token is sampled from the causal logits. The final text is therefore set by AR acceptance of drafts, the same mechanism the reviewer zeroed in Gemini 5bk0u2, Gemini 5jdhsl and Fable 61m629.
evidence: [247] engine code: '# Commit & Verification Pass (IS_CAUSAL=True: stores clean KV cache and computes verification logits)' then 'h_c = self.forward_block(cur_block_final, ..., is_causal=True ...)'.

[166] 'we commit m+1 tokens ... and sampling the next anchor from `logits_commit`'; [93] the causal pass is checked against the HF AR model ('Verification (is_causal=True) ... top1_match=100.0%').

'g_block_fast' (1 denoising step + commit) is used unless the previous block committed at least 6-7 tokens ([500], [543]), so many blocks get a single one-shot draft: the exact pattern failed in Fable 61m629.
